Automation Opportunity: - Scraping automated for ecommerce prices; SKU-match auto-suggested from the item-master mapping
Controls: - CTL-175 (ensure competitor-price data integrity & price-match governance.)
- CTL-400 (competition-law conduct — links to VS-129 / W2683); operational: Category Manager weekly collection-review
Pain Points / Risks: - **SKU-mismatch risk**: a competitor's "comparable" SKU isn't truly equivalent (different spec/pack), making the price comparison misleading; mitigated by the documented SKU-matching rule (equivalent spec, equivalent pack size)

- **Scraping-legality/ToS risk**: aggressive scraping violates competitor website ToS; mitigated by the compliant collection (respect robots.txt, use licensed third-party feeds, mystery-shopping within RA 10667 conduct limits)
System Touchpoints: - Price-intelligence platform (links to VS-27 / W113, VS-44 / market research) — the scraped/mystery-shopped dataset
- Item/SKU matching (links to VS-29 / W252, W403 competitor master) — the competitor-SKU-to-BuildRight-SKU mapping
- Pricing master (links to VS-29 / W289) — the BuildRight price for comparison

steps.activity: Pricing Analyst collects competitor prices: web scraping of competitor ecommerce sites, mystery-shop store visits for in-store prices, third-party price-intelligence feed; normalizes to BuildRight's SKU equivalents

Automation Opportunity: - Gap auto-flagged at >10%; margin-impact auto-computed before the decision
Controls: - CTL-175 (ensure competitor-price data integrity & price-match governance.)
- CTL-400 (price-change authorization — links to VS-08 / W40); CTL-108 (margin-floor guard — loss-making price prevention); operational: VP Merchandising sign-off on matches below the margin floor
Pain Points / Risks: - **Race-to-the-bottom risk**: matching every competitor cut erodes category margin to zero; mitigated by the margin-floor guard (no price below the documented floor) and the differentiate-option

- **Transient-promo-matching risk**: BuildRight matches a competitor's 1-week promo as a permanent price cut, surrendering margin after the competitor's promo ends; mitigated by the promo-vs-permanent distinction (match a permanent cut; counter a promo with a promo)
System Touchpoints: - Pricing master (links to VS-29 / W289, VS-08 / W40 price-change execution) — the price change
- Margin guard (links to VS-17 / W85 product costing, VS-158) — the margin-floor check before a match
- Analytics (links to VS-57 / W2230 margin analysis) — the margin-impact view

steps.activity: Category Manager reviews the >10%-gap SKUs; decides: match (lower price), differentiate (justify premium via value-add), or hold (transient competitor promo); executes the price change in the pricing master

Automation Opportunity: - Competitor-promo auto-detected from circular/social-media monitoring; threat-level auto-assessed
Controls: - CTL-400 (ensure controlled execution — Competitor Price Data Collection & Analysis (PA-57.1).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Late-detection risk**: a competitor promo is detected days after launch, ceding sales; mitigated by the weekly (not monthly) monitoring cadence and the social-media alert
- **Over-reaction risk**: BuildRight launches a costly counter-promo for a minor competitor event; mitigated by the threat-assessment (is the competitor's promo material to BuildRight's category?)
System Touchpoints: - Promo-intelligence (links to VS-57 / W2214, VS-58 / W2260 competitor promo intelligence) — the competitor-promo dataset
- Promo planning (links to VS-58 / W2238 coupon design, VS-14 / W13 promotions) — the counter-promo
- Analytics (links to VS-57 / W2234 promo ROI) — the counter-promo ROI view

steps.activity: Pricing Analyst monitors competitor promos (weekly ad circulars, social media, in-store signage); assesses the competitive threat; recommends BuildRight's counter-promo or hold

Controls: - CTL-400 (ensure controlled execution — Competitor Price Data Collection & Analysis (PA-57.1).)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Positioning-incoherence risk**: a category is positioned "premium" but priced at parity, confusing the customer; mitigated by the positioning-price alignment check

- **One-position-fits-all risk**: a single positioning for a category ignores format variation (a compact store may need a different position than a flagship); mitigated by the format-aware positioning where material
System Touchpoints: - Pricing strategy (links to VS-01 / W1 assortment, VS-29 / W289) — the category price-position
- Competitive data (links to VS-57 / W2214, W2219 basket comparison) — the positioning evidence
- Category P&L (links to VS-17 / W85, VS-101 merchandise financial planning) — the margin implication

steps.activity: VP Merchandising reviews each category's price position: price-leader, parity, premium; validates against the competitive data (W2214) and the category strategy; adjusts the positioning where the data warrants

Automation Opportunity: - Rules auto-fired within bands; conflict auto-detected; performance auto-reported
Controls: - CTL-400 (ensure controlled execution — Competitor Price Data Collection & Analysis (PA-57.1).)
- CTL-400 (price-change authorization — links to VS-08); CTL-108 (margin-floor guard — loss-making price prevention); operational: Category Manager monthly rule-review sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Rule-conflict risk**: two rules fire on the same SKU (competitor-follow lowers, inventory-clearance lowers further), producing an unintended deep discount; mitigated by the rule-precedence (one rule per SKU per period) and the conflict-check

- **Customer-trust risk**: too-frequent price changes (especially upward) erode customer trust ("the price is different every visit"); mitigated by the upward-change discipline (rare, justified) and the downward-change tolerance
System Touchpoints: - Pricing engine / rules (links to VS-29 / W289, VS-08 / W107 pricing hierarchy, W329 competitive tactical response) — the dynamic-pricing rules
- Competitor feed (links to VS-57 / W2214) — the competitor-price-follow input
- Inventory (links to VS-05 / W220 slow-moving) — the clearance-rule input

steps.activity: Pricing Analyst maintains the dynamic-pricing rules: competitor-price-follow rules (auto-adjust within a band), inventory-clearance rules (auto-markdown at threshold), time-based rules (happy-hour, slow-day); reviews rule performance and tunes

fields.Trigger: Quarterly comprehensive cycle — Market Basket Price Comparison

Controls: - CTL-175 (ensure competitor-price data integrity & price-match governance.)
- Operational: VP Merchandising quarterly basket sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Basket-relevance risk**: the 100-SKU basket doesn't match what customers actually compare (a basket of slow-movers no one notices); mitigated by the basket drawn from the high-velocity, high-comparison SKUs

- **Basket-positioning-vs-margin risk**: lowering the basket to look competitive erodes margin on the most-visible SKUs; mitigated by the basket-vs-margin joint view (the "loss-leader basket" funded by margin elsewhere)
System Touchpoints: - Basket benchmark (links to VS-57 / W2214, VS-44 / market research) — the 100-SKU basket
- Pricing master (links to VS-29 / W289) — the BuildRight basket prices
- Analytics (links to VS-27 / W113) — the basket-comparison visualization

steps.activity: Pricing Analyst compares BuildRight's 100-SKU benchmark basket (the high-visibility basket customers use to judge "expensive vs. cheap") vs. each competitor; identifies where BuildRight is above/below; recommends the basket-positioning adjustment

Automation Opportunity: - Elasticity auto-computed from the price-volume history; confounded-periods auto-flagged
Controls: - CTL-400 (ensure controlled execution — Competitor Price Data Collection & Analysis (PA-57.1).)
- Operational: Analytics Manager methodology sign-off; VP Merchandising review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Confounded-elasticity risk**: the elasticity model conflates the price effect with a concurrent promo or a competitor move; mitigated by the controlled-period selection (periods with only a price change, no confounders)
- **Stale-elasticity risk**: the elasticity from 2 years ago doesn't reflect a customer whose income/preferences shifted; mitigated by the semi-annual refresh
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (links to VS-27 / W113, W208 retail analytics) — the price-volume history for the elasticity model
- Pricing master (links to VS-29 / W289) — the historical prices
- Demand forecasting (links to VS-02 / W31) — the elasticity feeds the forecast

steps.activity: Analytics Manager computes the price-elasticity (the demand-response to a price change) for ~50–100 key SKUs from historical price-volume data; classifies elastic (price-sensitive) vs. inelastic (price-insensitive); informs the pricing strategy

fields.Trigger: Monthly reporting cycle — Competitor Pricing Intelligence Report

Automation Opportunity: - Report auto-assembled from the W2214–W2220 datasets; action-prompts auto-tagged
Controls: - CTL-400 (ensure controlled execution — Competitor Price Data Collection & Analysis (PA-57.1).)
- Operational: Category Manager monthly review; VP Merchandising escalation on unaddressed material moves
Pain Points / Risks: - **Report-as-shelfware risk**: the report is distributed but not acted on; mitigated by the action-prompt per finding (each material move carries a "Category Manager to decide by" tag)
- **Data-overload risk**: the report is too detailed for the Category Manager audience; mitigated by the executive-summary-first structure
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (links to VS-27 / W113) — the intelligence-report dataset
- Competitive intelligence (links to VS-33 / competitive intelligence, VS-57 / W2214–W2220) — the source data
- Distribution (links to VS-07 / W571) — the report distribution

steps.activity: Pricing Analyst compiles the monthly intelligence report: competitor price moves, promo activity, basket-position shift, BuildRight's positioning implication; distributes to Category Managers and VP Merchandising
